newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain must continue to cut deficit - BoS Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Spain must continue to cut deficit - BoS Rojo.

text.p: Bank of Spain Governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Tuesday it was reasonable to believe the Spanish consumer price index would end the year at 3.4 percent.
He also said it was essential that Spain continue cutting the budget deficit in years ahead.
He was speaking before the budget committee of the legislature.
"It is fundamental that (Spain) continue to reduce the public deficit in coming years because this is going to be the general approach," Rojo said.
Rojo said there are "elements of restriction" on the economy in the 1997 budget draft, which gave the Bank of Spain room to cut official rates by 50 basis points.

The Bank of Spain last cut its key money market rate on October 3, seizing its first chance after the government presented and approved the budget at the end of September. The budget must now be approved by the Parliament.

Rojo said in order to give the European single currency process more credibility, the countries that wanted to be part of it needed to continue reducing their budget deficit. Their aim should be one percent or less of deficit to GDP.
